He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami Hurricanes]] of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC). Wong earned third-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] honors as a [[senior (education)|senior]] in 2023, when he was also named the [[Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|ACC Player of the Year]]. He was selected by the Pacers in the second round of the [[2023 NBA draft]]. ==Early life== Born in [[Piscataway, New Jersey]], Wong played prep basketball at [[Notre Dame High School (New Jersey)|Notre Dame High School]] in [[Lawrenceville, New Jersey]] during his first two years.{{cite web|first=Rich|last=Fisher|title=Huge second half pushes Notre Dame boys basketball past Trenton|url=https://www.trentonian.com/sports/huge-second-half-pushes-notre-dame-boys-basketball-past-trenton/article_0bfbd5ca-ca74-5ce6-be10-792f3f8aaaf8.amp.html|work=[[The Trentonian]]|date=January 11, 2016|access-date=May 3, 2021|quote="Notre Dame also ran a more patient offense after breaking Trenton’s press [...] but the true eye-opener was Isaiah Wong, the freshman from South Brunswick [...]"|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210503143228/https://www.trentonian.com/sports/huge-second-half-pushes-notre-dame-boys-basketball-past-trenton/article_0bfbd5ca-ca74-5ce6-be10-792f3f8aaaf8.amp.html|archive-date=May 3, 2021|url-status=dead}} For his junior season, he transferred to [[Bonner & Prendergast Catholic High School]] in [[Drexel Hill, Pennsylvania]].{{cite web|first=David|last=Cordova|title=Isaiah Wong Draws A Lot of Attention With His Play|url=https://davesjoint.net/2018/07/02/isaiah-wong-draws-a-lot-of-attention-with-his-play/|work=Dave's Joint|date=July 2, 2018|access-date=May 2, 2021}} As a junior, he averaged 22.2 points, 6.5 rebounds and 3.6 assists per game, leading his team to the [[Philadelphia Catholic League]] regular season title, and was named Catholic League MVP.{{cite web|first=Matthew|last=De George|title=All-Delco Boys Basketball: Wong finds, conquers his challenge at Bonner & Prendergast|url=https://papreplive.com/2018/04/11/all-delco-boys-basketball-wong-finds-conquers-his-challenge-at-bonner-prendergast/|work=PA Prep Live|date=April 11, 2018|access-date=May 2, 2021}} In his senior season, Wong averaged 21.9 points, 7.5 rebounds and 2.5 assists per game. He led his team to the Class 4A state title game and repeated as Catholic League MVP.{{cite web|first=Matthew|last=De George|title=All-Delco Boys Basketball: Repeat season just as good as the first for Bonner's Wong|url=https://papreplive.com/2019/04/19/all-delco-boys-basketball-repeat-season-just-as-good-as-the-first-for-bonners-wong/|work=PA Prep Live|date=April 19, 2019|access-date=May 2, 2021}} He committed to playing college basketball for [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami (Florida)]] over offers from [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]], [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn]], [[Clemson Tigers men's basketball|Clemson]] and [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh]].{{cite web|first=Aaron|last=Carter|title=Bonner-Prendergast's Isaiah Wong commits to the University of Miami|url=https://www.inquirer.com/philly/sports/high_school/isaiah-wong-university-of-miami-commitment-bonner-prendergast-philadelphia-catholic-league-20180926.html|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=September 26, 2018|access-date=May 2, 2021}} ==College career== [[File:Isaiah Wong.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Wong with the [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami Hurricanes]]]] On February 9, 2020, Wong recorded a freshman season-high 27 points and 12 rebounds, making all 14 of his free throws, in a 102–95 win over [[2019–20 Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball team|Virginia Tech]] in triple overtime.{{cite web|first=Christopher|last=Stock|title=Isaiah Wong's 27-12 leads Miami to 102-95 3OT win over Hokies|url=https://247sports.com/college/miami/Article/Isaiah-Wongs-27-12-leads-Miami-Hurricanes-basketball-to-102-95-3OT-win-over-Virginia-Tech-Hokies-144090800/|work=[[247Sports]]|date=February 19, 2020|access-date=May 2, 2021}} As a freshman, he averaged 7.7 points and three rebounds per game.{{cite web|first=John|last=Reynolds|title=Canes Hoops: Isaiah Wong Profile|url=https://www.stateoftheu.com/2020/11/25/21719552/miami-hurricanes-basketball-isaiah-wong-canes-the-u-jim-larranaga|work=State of the U|date=November 25, 2020|access-date=May 2, 2021}} On January 16, 2021, Wong posted a career-high 30 points, seven rebounds and six assists in a 78–72 victory against [[2020–21 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|Louisville]].{{cite web|first=Christopher|last=Stock|title=Isaiah Wong's career-high 30 points helps Miami knock off No. 16 Louisville 78-72|url=https://247sports.com/college/miami/Article/Isaiah-Wongs-career-high-30-points-helps-Miami-Hurricanes-basketball-knock-off-No-16-Louisville-78-72-159423315/|work=[[247Sports]]|date=January 16, 2021|access-date=May 2, 2021}} As a sophomore, he averaged 17.1 points, 4.8 rebounds and 2.4 assists per game, earning third-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] honors.{{cite web|first=David|last=Furones|title=UM leading scorer Isaiah Wong announces NBA draft intentions |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-hurricanes/fl-sp-um-basketball-isaiah-wong-draft-20210414-wcdi72v47ra6xpirvlvb634p4i-story.html|work=[[Sun-Sentinel]]|date=April 14, 2021|access-date=May 2, 2021}}{{cite web|first=Michael|last=Yero|title=Isaiah Wong's Breakout Season Shouldn't Be Forgotten|url=https://www.305sports.net/isaiah-wongs-breakout-season-shouldnt-be-forgotten/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210309042135/https://www.305sports.net/isaiah-wongs-breakout-season-shouldnt-be-forgotten/|url-status=usurped|archive-date=March 9, 2021|website=305Sports.net|date=March 8, 2021|access-date=May 2, 2021}} On April 14, 2021, Wong [[NBA draft declaration|declared]] for the [[2021 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility. He ultimately returned for his junior season. Wong was named to the third-team All-ACC as a junior.{{cite press release|title=ACC Unveils 2021-22 Men's Basketball Awards|url=https://theacc.com/news/2022/3/6/athlete-awards-acc-unveils-2021-22-mens-basketball-awards.aspx|website=TheACC.com|publisher=[[Atlantic Coast Conference]]|date=March 7, 2022|access-date=March 7, 2022}} He was the second-leading scorer on the team, which advanced to the Elite Eight of the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2022 NCAA tournament]]. After the season, he again declared for the draft while maintaining his eligibility.{{cite news|first1=Jonathan|last1=Givony|first2=Jeff|last2=Borzello|name-list-style=and|title=NIL agent says Miami hoops star Isaiah Wong will enter transfer portal if NIL compensation isn't increased|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33823826|website=ESPN.com|date=April 28, 2022|access-date=April 29, 2022}} In 2023 he was named the [[Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|ACC Player of the Year]] and helped Miami reach their first-ever [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|Final Four]].{{cite web|first=Adam|last=Lichtenstein|title=Hurricanes' Isaiah Wong named ACC Player of the Year|url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-hurricanes/fl-sp-um-wong-acc-20230306-vobt6tc6wvb4ldspw3alei7wwa-story.html|website=SunSentinel.com|date=March 6, 2023|access-date=April 15, 2023}} ==Professional career== ===Indiana Pacers / Mad Ants (2023–2024)=== Wong was selected by the [[Indiana Pacers]] with the 55th overall pick in the second round of the [[2023 NBA draft]],{{cite web|first=Mike|last=Schiffman|title=Jordan Miller And Isaiah Wong Get Drafted In The Second Round Of The 2023 NBA Draft|url=https://www.stateoftheu.com/2023/6/23/23771224/miami-hurricanes-basektball-jordan-miller-and-isaiah-wong-drafted-in-second-round-of-2023-nba-draft|website=StateOfTheU.com|date=June 23, 2023|access-date=September 6, 2023}} subsequently joining the team for the [[2023 NBA Summer League]]. On July 3, 2023, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Pacers, splitting time with their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Indiana Mad Ants]].{{cite web|title=Pacers Sign Tshiebwe and Wong to Two-Way Contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-tshiebwe-and-wong-to-two-way-contracts|website=NBA.com|date=July 3, 2023|access-date=September 6, 2023}} He made his NBA debut in the [[2023 NBA In-Season Tournament championship game|2023 NBA In-Season Tournament final]], appearing briefly in the final minute of the game as the Pacers lost 109–123 to the [[Los Angeles Lakers|Lakers]]. ===Utah Jazz / Salt Lake City Stars (2024)=== On September 27, 2024, Wong signed with the [[Utah Jazz]],{{cite web|title=Utah Jazz Sign Taevion Kinsey and Isaiah Wong|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-taevion-kinsey-and-isaiah-wong|website=NBA.com|date=September 27, 2024|access-date=September 28, 2024}} but was waived on October 8.{{cite web|first=Jeremy|last=Rincon|title=Utah Jazz Waive Abmas, Kinsey, and Wong|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-waive-abmas-kinsey-and-wong|website=NBA.com|date=October 8, 2024|access-date=October 8, 2024}} On October 28, he joined their NBA G League affiliate [[Salt Lake City Stars]].{{cite web|title=Stars Announce 2024-25 Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/stars-announce-2024-25-training-camp-roster/n-6160474|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 28, 2024|access-date=November 2, 2024}} ===Charlotte Hornets / Greensboro Swarm (2024–2025)=== On December 2, 2024, Wong signed a two-way contract with the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite web|title=Hornets Sign Isaiah Wong To Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-sign-isaiah-wong-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=December 2, 2024|access-date=December 2, 2024}} On February 13, 2025, Wong was waived by the Hornets.{{cite web|title=Charlotte Hornets Waive Isaiah Wong|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/charlotte-hornets-waive-isaiah-wong|website=NBA.com|date=February 13, 2025|access-date=February 13, 2025}} ===Žalgiris Kaunas (2025)=== On February 26, 2025, Wong signed with Lithuanian club [[BC Žalgiris|Žalgiris Kaunas]] for the remainder of the season.{{cite web|title=Zalgiris adds scoring punch with Isaiah Wong|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/news/zalgiris-adds-scoring-punch-with-isaiah-wong/|website=EuroLeague|date=February 26, 2025|access-date=February 26, 2025}} On April 13 of the same year, he agreed on a three-year contract extension. After re-signing, Wong started getting less minutes from Žalgiris head coach [[Andrea Trinchieri]], and despite helping Žalgiris regain the LKL championship, with a change in the team's direction, Wong and Žalgiris mutually terminated the contract. ===Gran Canaria (2025–2026)=== On August 2, 2025, Wong signed with [[CB Gran Canaria|Gran Canaria]] of the [[Liga ACB]].{{Cite
